title: The universal form
hook: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's true form and is overwhelmed

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was wajh, the face found wherever you turn. Your line was no turn steps outside it.

Two armies are lined up, ready to fight. Between them sits a chariot with two people in it. One is Arjuna, a warrior who has lost his nerve. The other is his charioteer, Krishna, who has spent a long conversation teaching him. By now Arjuna has heard enough to suspect that his driver is far more than a driver. So he asks: if it's possible, let me see you as you really are. It's a request people make of friends, of lovers, of God. This time, it's granted.
screen: `TWO ARMIES. ONE CHARIOT.` → `LET ME SEE YOU AS YOU ARE.` → `THE REQUEST IS GRANTED.`

segments.voice: This is chapter eleven of the Bhagavad Gita, a Hindu scripture, and it unfolds in four movements. First, the eyes. Krishna tells Arjuna that he can't see this with his ordinary eyes, so he gives him a divine eye, a new way of seeing. Awe here isn't something you squint at; you need different eyes for it. Second, the sight. Arjuna sees the whole universe gathered in one body: countless faces and eyes, ornaments and weapons, the gods themselves, all of it in one form. A narrator reaches for the brightness: if the light of a thousand suns rose in the sky at once, he says, that might come near the splendor of it. Third, the shaking. Arjuna's hair stands on end. He bows his head and folds his hands. As the vision goes on, it turns terrifying: worlds and warriors rushing into blazing mouths like rivers into the sea. Arjuna admits he's lost his bearings and can find no peace. Fourth, the way back. Near the end Arjuna says he's glad to have seen what he had never seen before, and yet his mind is shaken with fear. He asks to see the familiar form again, the one he knows. Krishna gently returns to it, and Arjuna says he is himself again. That's the honesty of this chapter. The vision is real, and it's too much. Hindu readers hear many things here, but the story never pretends that seeing everything is comfortable.
screen: `A DIVINE EYE TO SEE WITH.` · `THE WHOLE UNIVERSE IN ONE FORM.` · `HAIR ON END. NO PEACE.` · `SHOW ME THE FAMILIAR FORM AGAIN.` · then, large: `OVERWHELMED.`

segments.voice: Find the biggest thing you can see from where you are, a long street, a crowd, every leaf on one full tree, and try to take in all of it at once; notice that you can't, and let that be fine. When it gets to be too much, come back to something small and familiar, your hand or the floor, the way Arjuna asked for the form he knew, and then look out again.
Arjuna. The warrior who asked to see Krishna as he really is, and was left overwhelmed by the whole universe in one body. Today's word.
Your line: overwhelmed. Arjuna saw everything, then asked for the face he knew. Day one thousand nine.

howItsDone: Hindus read and recite the Bhagavad Gita, and the vision of chapter eleven is painted and sculpted as Krishna's universal form, often shown with many heads and arms.

chat.says: In the Gita, was Arjuna happy to see Krishna's universal form?
options: Glad and shaken at once: it was too much, so he asked for the familiar form.
Only happy: seeing everything gave him perfect peace right away.
Only angry: he felt tricked, and he refused to look at it at all.
chat.meaning: Arjuna's hair stands on end and he finds no peace. Glad yet shaken with fear, he asks for the familiar form, and Krishna gently returns to it.

notes: All Gita material paraphrased (Arnold 1885 available but exact wording not certain to this writer). Verse ranges: request 11.3–4; divine eye 11.8; the vision and the thousand suns 11.10–13 (spoken by Sanjaya, called 'a narrator'); hair on end, bowed head, folded hands 11.14; rivers into the sea and no peace 11.24–28; 'seen what was never seen before', joy and fear, request for the familiar (four-armed) form 11.45–46; return to gentle human form, 'I am myself again' 11.50–51. Confirm verse numbers.
The 'familiar form' is simplified: 11.46 asks for the four-armed form, then 11.50–51 the gentle human form. Confirm the simplification.
'Hindu readers hear many things here': soft; confirm.
